headline: 13.79 percent of Ward 33's licensed food stores are chains, the lowest share in the city.
summary:
Albany Park, Irving Park, Avondale and North Park sit inside a ward whose strongest marks come from neighborhood life rather than city government, one that lands squarely in the city's middle, 25th overall out of fifty, scoring 45.91. The ward's bars carry a median Google rating of 4.75, the best score among the 45 wards with rated bars, and its houses of worship rate close behind at 4.9. Places across the ward rate second-best in the city overall, at 4.73 out of 5. Chain outlets make up just under 14 percent of the ward's licensed food stores, the smallest share in Chicago, with the rest independently owned. The ward also reports fewer traffic-crash injuries than all but two others citywide, and ranks third for how many home languages are spoken there, a mark tied to Albany Park's long history as a landing spot for immigrant and refugee families.

The weak points are almost all city services, not neighborhood character. Ward 33 lands 48th of 50 on both 311 response time and pothole repair time, and dead last, 50th of 50, on the share of its yearly menu money actually spent on projects instead of left idle. The ward has no libraries mapped inside its boundaries either, also last in the city. Registered murals rank 48th of 49, and total place reviews rank 49th of 50. Ward 33 pairs an active bar and worship scene and mostly independent local businesses with a ward that trails most of the city on infrastructure and how fast basic requests get handled.
reading_the_rankings:
A couple of these numbers need their caveats attached. Ward 33's lowest chain-store share in the city, just under 14 percent, is pulled from a business-license field tied to the ward as it stood whenever each license was filed. The ward's boundaries changed in 2023, recently enough that some of the older licenses behind that number describe a differently shaped ward than the one that exists now. The same recent redraw sits behind the last-place finish on menu money spent, where only 55.9 percent of the ward's roughly $1.5 million annual allotment went to committed projects in the latest full year.

The near-last finish on total place reviews reads harsher than the real numbers support. Thirty-six of the fifty wards come in less than two points apart from Ward 33 on this measure, and citywide this measure barely spans two points from top to bottom, so the rank here is sharper than the gap it is actually measuring.

news.headline: Homeless Encampment Fight Overshadows Long-Awaited Ronan Park Plaza Debut
news.note: A ribbon-cutting for Ronan Park's new riverside plaza was disrupted by dueling protests over an unhoused encampment nearby, with Ald. Rossana Rodriguez-Sanchez among the officials present.

news.headline: ICE Crash And Arrest In Albany Park Leaves Neighbors Furious: 'We Should Not Have To Live Like This'
news.note: Federal immigration agents crashed an SUV into a bystander's car while making an arrest near Lawrence and Kedzie, prompting a neighborhood protest the next evening.
